setup: **No key in first messages.** Every download includes 14 days of Pro, so they can try everything; the messages offer a free licence if they reply.
**When someone replies, make their licence:** a 100%-off discount on Ringo Pro, usable once, named after them (e.g. `MAYA`). Send it with the "They said yes" reply.
**Pace:** 3–5 a day, each by hand. Check the first line of each message against its source before sending.
**One follow-up** after 7 days with no answer, then let it go.

messages.label: Email
messages.subject: A Mac app for your next round-up, if it earns a place
messages.body:
Hi Maya,

I saw your "9 Mac Apps I Use Every Day" video, and liked that you showed each one in use rather than reading out a list. I make a small Mac app called Ringo, and I think it might fit a future round-up.

It opens your apps in a ring around the cursor: hold a key, flick toward an app, let go. No aiming at a Dock icon at the bottom of the screen.

90-second demo: https://youtu.be/EXAMPLE

It comes with 14 days of Pro, so you can try everything. If you'd like to keep it, just reply and I'll send you a free licence.
No strings: if it's not for you, no need to reply.

Thanks,
Alex
ringo.example

messages.label: Tagline
messages.body: Your apps in a ring around your cursor: hold a key, flick, let go.

messages.label: Description
messages.body:
Ringo opens your apps in a ring around the pointer, wherever it is. Hold a key (or the middle mouse button), flick toward the one you want and let go: only the direction counts.

Native Swift, about 20 MB, no account. Free to download with 14 days of Pro; Pro is a one-time purchase.

Hi,

A suggestion for the newsletter: Ringo, a Mac launcher I build on my own.

• Your apps in a ring around the cursor: hold a key, flick, let go
• Only the direction counts, so no aiming at icons
• Native, about 20 MB, no account
• macOS 14+, Apple silicon and Intel
• Free with 14 days of Pro; Pro is a one-time purchase

Site: https://ringo.example
Demo (90 s): https://youtu.be/EXAMPLE
Screenshots attached. Happy to answer anything or send a licence.

Thanks,

replies.title: They said yes, or asked for the licence
replies.body:
Thanks [name]! Here's your free licence: go to ringo.example/buy and enter the code [THEIR CODE] at checkout. It comes to $0, and your key arrives by email.

Hold the shortcut anywhere to open the ring. Anything odd or missing, tell me and I'll fix it.

If you do end up linking it anywhere, this link lets me see it was you: ringo.example/?utm_source=[THEIR NAME]

replies.title: They asked about a giveaway
replies.body: Happy to! I can give you 3 licences for your audience. Tell me how you'd like them and when it goes out, so I'm around to answer questions.

replies.title: They asked for payment
replies.body: Thanks for the details. I'm one person building Ringo and don't have a budget for paid placements right now, so I'll have to pass. The free licence is yours either way.

replies.title: They mentioned it
replies.body: Thank you, [name]! Really appreciate you taking the time. I'll share it, and I'm answering any questions in the comments.

replies.title: They said it's not for them
replies.body: No worries at all, thanks for taking a look. Keep the licence if you like.

replies.title: One follow-up after 7 days
replies.body: Hi [name], just making sure this didn't get buried. No pressure at all; the offer stands if you ever want to try Ringo. https://youtu.be/EXAMPLE
